why: Plugin MARKETPLACES this pack once registered, or that a tool registered on its own, and that should no longer exist on a machine. Registration is additive everywhere: Install-Provider-Starter-Settings.ps1 only ever ADDS to extraKnownMarketplaces, and no provider removes a marketplace when the tool behind it is uninstalled. So a registration outlives its tool forever, and worse, it PROPAGATES -- Grok inherits Claude's marketplace list, so one dead entry in ~/.claude becomes a failing entry in ~/.grok that the user never registered at all. RETIRED-SKILLS.json solves exactly this problem for skills; this is the same idea for marketplaces.
measured: 2026-08-27 on the maintainer's machine: claude-mem had been uninstalled and 1.29 GB of its payload already reclaimed, yet 'thedotmack' was still registered in Claude's known_marketplaces.json AND settings.json, still cloned at 140 MB under plugins/marketplaces, still present as FOUR orphaned 140 MB temp clones, and had been synced into ~/.grok/marketplace-cache, where grok reported it as `thedotmack (0 plugins) [error] Git sync failed: failed to lock cache`. Every one of those is a leftover of a tool the user removed weeks earlier.
scope: Removal is limited to a marketplace whose name AND git URL both match an entry below, and which contributes NO enabled plugin. A marketplace that still has an enabled plugin is reported, never touched -- the point is to clear the dead, not to disable something in use.

retired.reason: claude-mem was uninstalled. Its marketplace registration survived in Claude, kept a 140 MB clone plus four orphaned temp clones on disk, and propagated into Grok, which then failed to sync it on every start.
